parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile parent layer with a comparatively protective state. Parent exposures are traveller-facing and partly universal: binary-only passport/visa markers with confiscation reports, an entry cable permitting refusal on sex discrepancy and lifetime fraud ineligibility, a federal ban on gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities, conversion-therapy-style custody policy, and official threat-framing — with litigation pending but no operative remedy. Eight governments issued travel advisories. The state adds real mitigation: explicit gender-identity discrimination bans with enforced remedies, open identity documents, no state facility or presentation offence, a sanctuary city, and a July 2026 low-risk tier. State protections do not pre-empt federal facilities, documents or custody, so tier-1 parent exposures keep this well below Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Parent: X markers halted Feb 2025; new visas/passports M or F only; cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked abroad; foreign advisories issued. Documented.
entry_documents.protection: State issues X on licences/IDs since 2020 and allows birth-certificate change; but state documents do not govern federal entry. Litigation against the foreign ministry is unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home passport meets federal visa/entry screening first; state document openness never reaches the border desk.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Parent: corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policy (haircut, hormone removal, substitute psychiatric treatment) from 2026; immigration custody reports beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans detainees; prisoner counts unpublished since 2025. Documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State is graded low-risk for targeting trans adults; no state custody abuse documented. Hate-crime statute covers gender identity federally.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor entering federal or immigration custody leaves the protective state layer entirely; no documented shield.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Parent executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity — a universal exposure in federal buildings nationally. State has no facility ban; another state's trespass arrest (Mar 2025) shows enforcement risk elsewhere. Documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State: no facility ban; largest city requires gender-neutral bathrooms in public buildings; December 2022 regulation defines sex to include gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: City/state facility tolerance cannot displace the federal rule in federally owned or funded settings the visitor will use.

care_services.exposure: Parent: executive order calls gender-affirming care 'mutilation'; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records; proposed rules bar insurance reimbursement for trans under-18s; LGBTQ youth crisis services shut down. Documented.
care_services.protection: State: adult gender-affirming care lawful, no adult prohibition; largest city sanctuary order (Oct 2023) shields travellers from outside enforcement and deprioritises restrictive enforcement.
care_services.interaction: City shield mitigates state/national care restrictions for a visiting family, but is an executive order of uncertain durability against federal pressure; not_documented as tested against federal process.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parent: counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo lists 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating views; orders describe care as mutilation; 66% public support for birth-sex document rules. Documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State governor called sports-bill supporters 'extremists' and vetoed a 2022 anti-trans measure; state graded low-risk for targeting trans adults.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State rhetoric offsets local police posture but not federal agencies executing national orders.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent: EO directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; care for minors banned in 27 states; hospital-record subpoenas. A visiting trans minor or parent faces national hostility framing. Documented.
minors_guardians.protection: State: parental birth-certificate change from 18; city bars youth-serving organisations from discriminating; conversion therapy restricted; adult care lawful.
minors_guardians.interaction: City sanctuary order expressly shields travellers from outside enforcement, but federal charging authority over 'facilitation' is untested; a minor's passport still follows the binary federal rule.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State has no hate-crime statute reaching anti-LGBTQ violence (2008 struck-down law never reinstated); thin recourse if assaulted. Federal bias reporting shows sexual-orientation bias at 1/7–1/5 of single-bias incidents. Documented partially.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state human-rights commission investigates identity discrimination with damages and stop orders; no organised targeting documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists federally and via the commission, but state-level bias-violence prosecution lacks a statutory hook.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Parent passport suit, EO challenges and health rules unresolved; successive litigation has not yet produced relief — recurring findings without remedy. Unknowns: how the entry cable is applied case-by-case; detention placement specifics for this state.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Commission remedies (stop orders, training, damages) documented as operating since 2018; anti-discrimination ban in force since June 2023; sports bills repeatedly blocked or stalled.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working state anti-discrimination enforcement cannot remedy federal document, facility or custody exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: that anchor shows a nationwide birth-sex facility rule upheld with complaints routinely rejected and no offence-free margin. Here the parent facility ban is narrower (government-funded single-sex settings), entry/document friction is conditional rather than universal, and the state layer documents operating anti-discrimination remedies, no facility ban and a low-risk grading.

Closest match. Like Denvara, a government-funded birth-sex facility rule bites visitors while the wider public is unremarkably polite and no presentation offence exists. This case adds a heavier document/entry regime (marker refusal, confiscation reports, fraud-ineligibility consideration) and federal custody conversion-therapy policy, but also explicit state protections and enforced remedies absent from Denvara.

Similar protective scaffolding: equality law, functioning courts, accepted foreign documents, no facility restriction, isolated prosecuted assault, custody placement undocumented. Rated above it because the parent adds universal federal facility exclusion, an entry-document regime with stranded-traveller reports, custody abuse and official threat-framing that no state measure offsets.

Below 0.65-B: Iveran's parent regime has no trans-specific border or facility restriction and a working national complaint process, with hostility purely social and remedied locally. Here the parent itself imposes document, facility and custody exposures with litigation unresolved, so local remedies cannot lift the score into Reduced Risk.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: a hostile federal layer and a protective state layer that do not cancel. Entry runs through the parent's binary document and visa regime, where mismatched markers risk refusal, confiscation or a fraud finding — litigation is pending but grants no present relief. In federally owned or funded single-sex settings the birth-sex rule applies regardless of the state's inclusive regulations; the state's anti-discrimination ban, X-markers, gender-neutral city bathrooms and sanctuary order operate only below that line. Custody follows the federal conversion-therapy-style policy if the visitor enters federal or immigration detention. Street-level and service exposure in this state is comparatively low, but the absence of a state hate-crime statute thins recourse. Net: everyday state life is tolerable, federal chokepoints are not — Elevated Risk.
